title: csm-orchestrate Approach Adversarial Review and Correction Finding

tldr.content: The agreed csm-orchestrate approach is conceptually sound but not yet implementation-ready. Its largest gaps are the absence of a formal parent/child invocation contract, capability manifest, requirement-to-evidence schema, approval binding, route-phase schema, and final-review phase-insertion rules. Correct it by making the orchestrator a receipt-gated outer loop: compile each incoming approach phase into one thin slice, execute only declared routes, validate technical and functional evidence, adversarially review the result, and let final review create bounded new phases when gaps remain.

executiveSummary.content:
This DEEP hybrid audit reviewed the current agreed approach, all 13 skill contracts, shared schemas/runtimes, edge inventory, producer descriptors, prior research, and lifecycle evidence.

```text
approach -> phase compiler -> phase acceptance ledger -> route/approval
                                      |                    |
                                      v                    v
                                child receipt -> typed/evidence gates
                                      |                    |
                                      +-> adversarial review -> final review
                                                                  |
                                             accepted next phase <-+
                                             new remediation phase <- gap
```

The approach correctly preserves sibling ownership and demands final review, but it currently mixes design intent with guarantees that the repository does not yet provide. Run IDs, paths, `BLOCKED`, recovery, approvals, and child receipts differ among skills. The approach must explicitly normalize or adapt these differences, and it must distinguish a phase being implemented from a phase being accepted.

keyFindings.content:
K1 [supported] The approach correctly makes csm-orchestrate an outer control plane rather than duplicating sibling domain logic. [ref-approach][ref-readme][ref-boundaries]

K2 [supported] Incoming `csm-grill` phases need compilation into runtime phase objects with thin-slice scope, route, acceptance signals, evidence, approvals, and checkpoints; the current approach states this but lacks a phase schema and phase identity rules. [ref-approach][ref-grill][ref-final]

K3 [supported] A formal host invocation contract is missing: no shared definition specifies how the parent invokes a child, passes inputs, captures output, handles timeout, assigns child IDs, or distinguishes transport failure from child failure. [ref-capabilities][ref-edge][ref-approach]

K4 [supported] Capability and approval metadata are insufficiently formalized for safe automatic dispatch; existing skill descriptors do not consistently declare input schemas, effects, permissions, retryability, idempotency, recovery, parallelism, or review obligations. [ref-capabilities][ref-build][ref-upload]

K5 [supported] Requirement coverage and evidence entailment need their own typed records; child success, test success, or a narrative receipt cannot prove the user outcome. [ref-approach][ref-build][ref-review][ref-final]

K6 [supported] Technical correctness and functional correctness must remain separate, and the final review must be mandatory; the approach needs an explicit gate-order contract and failure-to-new-phase transition. [ref-approach][ref-build][ref-bdd][ref-review]

K7 [supported] Long-horizon execution must preserve route-level checkpoints while respecting skill-specific recovery; a generic outer `BLOCKED -> RECOVER` rule cannot override terminal child blockers or non-resumable skills. [ref-lifecycle][ref-autoresearch][ref-grill][ref-python]

K8 [partially-supported] Bounded phase remediation and selective parallelism are plausible, but safe limits, idempotency, compensation, phase insertion ordering, and duplicate-side-effect protection remain unimplemented and unmeasured. [ref-approach][ref-edge][ref-evals]

K9 [supported] The approach contains a run-ID/path/terminal-status compatibility risk that must be resolved before implementation; the current repository has conflicting native skill prose and shared JSON schema conventions. [ref-compatibility][ref-envelope][ref-approach]

K10 [unverifiable] Implementing the approach will improve end-to-end agent correctness, productivity, autonomy, latency, or cost. [ref-evals]

detailSections.content:
### Phase compilation
An incoming approach is not itself an executable route. The orchestrator needs a compiler that turns each approach phase into a versioned phase object: `phaseId`, goal, requirement IDs, thin-slice scope, non-goals, route nodes, dependencies, input artifacts, expected outputs, acceptance signals, technical gates, functional scenarios, adversarial-review level, approval requirements, side effects, retry policy, checkpoint policy, and completion status. A phase may map to multiple skills and must not be treated as one child invocation.

### Parent/child invocation
Define a host contract before automatic dispatch. It must bind parent run ID, child run ID, route edge, skill/version/digest, input artifact IDs and digests, permissions, approvals, timeout, cancellation, retry key, output channel, receipt schema, and failure taxonomy. Transport failure, child failure, policy refusal, incomplete evidence, and evaluator failure must remain distinct. The current edge inventory provides lineage and schemas but not the full invocation contract.

### Capability and approval normalization
Extend or complement the discovery manifest with per-skill inputs, outputs, entrypoint, activation predicate, permissions, effects, approval class, review level, retryability, idempotency, parallelism, recovery, and terminal behavior. Bind approvals to parent run, child run, phase/edge, exact scope, artifact digest, approver, issue/expiry, consumption, and revocation. Metadata must not be treated as authorization; the host enforces it.

### One-shot correctness
At intake, preserve the exact ask and create an acceptance ledger. Each row needs requirement ID, normalized interpretation, criticality, risk, non-goal, observable acceptance signal, evidence kind, responsible route, reviewer, and status. Every child result maps evidence to rows. `VERIFIED` requires all critical rows supported by current technical, functional, or explicitly approved human evidence. Unresolved, stale, contradicted, or waived rows remain visible.

### Adversarial review
For every material child result, create a fresh reviewer view containing the ask, requirement rows, output, evidence, tool/action receipt, and expected acceptance signals, but not producer rationale. Attack omissions, unsupported claims, citation entailment, scope creep, stale/duplicate artifacts, unsafe actions, unauthorized effects, false completion, and invalid assumptions. Use lightweight independent review for ordinary results; delegate high-risk repository/security/public-interface review to csm-review or csm-review-python. The final review is always mandatory and must verify functional fulfillment and technical soundness.

### Technical and functional gate order
Use a fixed outer order: child artifact/schema/ownership/digest validation; requirement/evidence reconciliation; technical gates; functional scenarios; adversarial acceptance; final outcome review. Technical gates cover syntax, types, schemas, compatibility, security, protected paths, reproducibility, and artifact integrity. Functional gates cover normal, boundary, invalid, failure, refusal, recovery, partial-completion, and user-visible outcome scenarios. A technical pass cannot mask functional failure, and functional plausibility cannot override technical failure.

### Final-review phase insertion
If final review finds a gap, it must produce a new `phaseId` rather than silently editing history. The new phase records the requirement delta, reason, route, owner, approvals, acceptance signals, parent phase, insertion point, and remediation budget. It enters the same route, technical, functional, adversarial, checkpoint, and final-review loop. It cannot bypass completed evidence, reset retry budgets, or repeat non-idempotent side effects without reconciliation.

### Long-horizon state
The parent cursor should store current phase, route graph revision, ledger digest, active edge, completed child receipts, pending approvals, checkpoint, retry budget, side effects, blockers, and next safe transition. Route state, artifact lifecycle, verification status, and child state must be separate. A recoverable parent blocker cannot convert a terminal child policy blocker into a retry. Non-resumable skills require a new child run and explicit re-entry.

### Current implementation blockers
Before implementation, resolve the canonical run-ID grammar, path authority, receipt composition, approval object, capability manifest, phase schema, requirement/evidence schema, invocation contract, route replay/fault-injection suite, and whether the host can actually invoke sibling skills. The agreed approach currently names these dependencies but does not define their acceptance contracts.

recommendation.content:
Correct the approach with these mandatory invariants:

1. Add a `csm-orchestrate-phase/1` contract that compiles each incoming approach phase into an independently executable thin slice.
2. Add a `csm-orchestrate-requirement/1` ledger and evidence-link model; never derive completion from prose or child status.
3. Add a `csm-orchestrate-capabilities/1` manifest and `csm-orchestrate-invocation/1` host contract; fail closed when skill metadata or invocation semantics are missing.
4. Add a route-level approval object bound to parent/child/phase/edge, exact scope, artifact digest, approver, expiry, consumption, and revocation.
5. Add a parent orchestration cursor and receipt that references child artifacts without taking ownership.
6. Make final review mandatory and allow it to append a new bounded remediation phase with explicit lineage and budget.
7. Enforce separate technical and functional gates, then adversarial acceptance, then final review.
8. Normalize run IDs, paths, statuses, retry, recovery, and terminal semantics through explicit adapters; do not impose one generic recovery meaning on every skill.
9. Start automatic dispatch only after route replay, interruption, retry, duplicate-side-effect, approval-bypass, stale-artifact, and evaluator-failure tests pass.

These are correction requirements for a future implementation, not implementation work performed by this research run.

unverifiedClaims.content:
Decision-blocking: the host invocation mechanism for sibling skills is not defined or demonstrated.

Decision-blocking: the repository does not yet provide one uniform capability manifest, approval contract, phase schema, or requirement/evidence schema.

Material risk: shared schema and native skill prose conflict on run IDs, paths, terminal states, and recovery semantics.

Material risk: the exact boundary between the orchestrator’s final review and csm-review’s repository audit authority needs an adapter contract.

Material risk: phase insertion after final review can create dependency cycles or repeat side effects unless the phase graph has immutable parentage, ordering, and idempotency rules.

Material risk: independent adversarial review can itself be incomplete or anchored unless reviewer context, calibration, and disagreement handling are specified.

Informational: current repository tests establish pieces of artifact and lifecycle behavior, not complete outer-loop behavior.

Unverifiable: productivity, autonomy, cost, latency, and correctness improvements without controlled repository-local evaluation.

processAppendix.content:
Triage: DEEP, hybrid. Scope: audit the agreed csm-orchestrate approach against all current repository skill norms and the preceding architecture/assurance findings, then add adversarial-review and final-phase insertion correctness.

Research tracks: five independent read-only tracks covered capability metadata, lifecycle/ownership conflicts, requirement/evidence assurance, adversarial/technical/functional review, and long-horizon route control. No repository code was executed and no files other than this run-owned finding were intended for persistence.

Challenge: the independent challenger upheld the outer-control-plane boundary but downgraded phase-compiler, invocation-contract, and final-review-loop claims where the approach already stated the policy but lacked formal schema/enforcement. It identified unpinned citations, authoritative JSON mismatch, phase-cycle safety, approval authority, review-boundary, calibration, and schema-registration gaps. These corrections are incorporated.

Judge: independent final judge scored factual accuracy 0.87, citation accuracy 0.66, completeness 0.91, clarity 0.91; fail on citation accuracy. The judge found repository-origin URLs unpinned, vague/bundled locators, and a distinction needed between reference-ID resolution and substantive citation entailment. Those residual citation limitations remain explicitly disclosed.

Verification: nine material claims are represented with verdicts; all citation IDs resolve to defined references; eight section keys and projection order are present; no declared artifacts exist; no credentials or personal data are included. The prior approach remains unchanged and this finding provides correction guidance only.
